annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'He is quiet she is shamefaced', has no anagram indicator: HE IS + P + SHE has the right letters but no word signals rearranging them, so a word seems lost in OCR
annotationWithheld.clue: He is quiet she is shamefaced

clue.text: This oil's a distillation for a medical condition

indicators.note: a distillation reworks a liquid into a new form, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: the word oil with its s, taken as letters

explanation.surface: Inhaling a distilled oil is offered as the cure for some ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distillation' signals that THIS OILS A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Halitosis is the clinical name for chronic bad breath, a recognised ailment.

clue.text: Provide proper directions in the first place

indicators.note: the compass points are to be placed first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: E and N are compass directions, east and north
due means fitting or proper, as in due respect

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give correct instructions from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' supplies two compass points, and 'in the first place' fixes them at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or furnish someone with a quality, a formal synonym of supply.

clue.text: Though incurable, I can get round a physician

indicators.note: to get round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: I can expands to I'm able
a medic is a doctor or physician

explanation.surface: A patient with no cure still thinks they can talk a doctor round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I can' is expanded to its long form (I am able, shortened), and 'get round' wraps that phrase about the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immedicable cannot be healed by medicine, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Is opposed to turning over the soil

indicators.note: soil being turned over is churned up, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone objects to digging the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' looks like gardening but rearranges THE SOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hostile to an idea means being against it, unfriendly towards it.

clue.text: Former tax on intemperance

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: An old duty was charged on heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess is overindulgence, the lack of moderation that intemperance names.

clue.text: English set off on a sort of trip

parts.note: to go is to set off or depart

explanation.surface: An Englishman leaves on some kind of journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works through the phrase 'ego trip', a bout of self-indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an act done to boost one's own self-importance.

clue.text: Devastation — but a hundred stay calm somehow

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: somehow suggests some unspecified way of arranging, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Disaster strikes, yet a hundred people manage to keep their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges C with STAY CALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a violent upheaval or disaster causing ruin.

clue.text: Fly up and around the north with its aid?

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps about the other

parts.note: to soar is to fly upwards
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A pilot rises and circles towards the north, guided by an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts SOAR round N. The definition leans on the surface: sonar is the aid that lets a vessel find its way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar is the echo-sounding equipment that ships and submarines use to navigate and locate objects.

clue.text: Having dressed, many left on time

parts.note: C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many
AD, anno Domini, marks a span of time, the Christian era

explanation.surface: Once fully dressed, a crowd departed punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' as C is a crossword convention: a hundred is a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is a past participle of clothe, meaning wearing clothes.

clue.text: Paradoxically, it's more fun working it out

definitions.text: Paradoxically, it's more fun working it out

indicators.note: working something out means solving it by moving its parts, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the word it with its s, taken as letters

explanation.surface: Puzzling over the solution is more enjoyable than getting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working it out' rearranges ITS MORE FUN; the whole clue is the joke that bad luck is, paradoxically, more fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortune is bad luck, which is ironically described here as more fun.

clue.text: An abstainer with objective — to be there!

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A non-drinker with a purpose exclaims about turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: TT (teetotal) for an abstainer is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to be present at an event.

clue.text: Harmonising — and with small trumpet I improvise, in C

indicators.note: to improvise is to make something up freely, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: cor. is the abbreviation for cornet, a small trumpet, so a shortened cornet

explanation.surface: A musician harmonises, playing a little trumpet and jamming in the key of C.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improvise' rearranges AND, COR and I with C; 'small' signals the shortened form of cornet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in accord means agreeing, being in harmony with someone.

clue.text: Handle it in a careless way and get wiped out!

indicators.note: something done in a careless way is messed about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Mishandle something and you will be destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'careless way' rearranges HANDLE IT IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: To be annihilated is to be destroyed completely, utterly defeated.

clue.text: Redeploy / scout hence, seeking arms-bearer

indicators.note: redeploying troops moves them about, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A scout is sent off again to find a man to carry weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redeploy' rearranges SCOUT HENCE. 'arms' means heraldic arms, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield on which a coat of arms is displayed in heraldry.

clue.text: Emphasise importance of the subway

definitions.meaning: to stress something, as by drawing a rule beneath it

explanation.surface: Someone stresses how much the metro matters.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline is to stress something; split in two, the word describes an underground railway line.

clue.text: A beast — as even I can be

parts.note: yet means even, as in yet more

explanation.surface: A brute, one that even the speaker could turn into.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the abominable snowman, a legendary creature of the Himalayas.

clue.text: Historian finding priest at cathedral, robed in brown

indicators.note: something robed in a colour is wrapped in it, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: tan is a light brown
Rev, Reverend, is the title of a priest
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A clergyman at a cathedral is found wearing brown vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'robed in' wraps the colour around the clergyman and the cathedral, the small English city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: G. M. Trevelyan was a celebrated English historian of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Put into service though not in mint condition

explanation.surface: Something deployed though no longer brand new.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means employed for a purpose, and also second-hand rather than fresh.

clue.text: Cavity at the bottom of the sea where kippers could be found?

indicators.note: at signals that one piece sits right next to the other

parts.note: the seabed is the floor of the ocean
a chamber is an enclosed space or cavity

explanation.surface: A hollow on the ocean floor where smoked herrings lurk.
explanation.walkthrough: Kippers look like smoked fish, but a kipper is also British slang for someone having a nap (a kip).
explanation.definitionFit: A bedchamber is a bedroom, where people sleeping could be found.

clue.text: A no-ball decision could rule this out

definitions.text: A no-ball decision could rule this out

parts.words: A no-ball decision could rule this out
parts.note: no-ball looks like a cricket umpire's call, but read as a decision to hold no ball (a formal dance), it would cancel the activity

explanation.surface: An umpire's call of an illegal delivery settles the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery; here 'ball' means a dance party.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving rhythmically to music is what a ball is held for.

clue.text: Bug on rose? Spray around and move top-soil to make it flourish

indicators.note: spraying scatters droplets everywhere, so these letters are scattered into a new order
the top of a word is its opening letter, and it is to be moved away

explanation.surface: A gardener sprays an aphid-ridden rose and turns the soil to help it thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray around' rearranges the first three words, and 'move top' takes the first letter of soil out of that pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To bourgeon (or burgeon) is to put out buds, to grow and thrive.

clue.text: Patent covering tin-opener

parts.note: over can mean covering, as in a lid over a jar

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A registered invention involves a lid for a can opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like an invention licence but is the adjective meaning plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent and overt both mean open and obvious, not concealed.

clue.text: Let a scout leader in to show the way

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Let a scout leader in to show the way', yields LEASD: LEAD or LED with A and S inside cannot give the extra E of LEASED, so a word or letter seems lost or misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Let a scout leader in to show the way

clue.text: With reluctance, goes to a doctor —- a warning sign

indicators.note: goes to means one piece is attached on after the other

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
er is the noise of someone hesitating reluctantly

explanation.surface: Someone reluctantly visits a doctor about a symptom.
explanation.walkthrough: AMBER is the cautionary traffic light between green and red.
explanation.definitionFit: An amber traffic light warns drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Hand in foot, doing this job? Quite the reverse

definitions.text: Hand in foot, doing this job? Quite the reverse

parts.words: Hand in foot, doing this job? Quite the reverse
parts.note: hand in glove suggests partnership, but reversed it pictures a worker who holds a foot in hand all day

explanation.surface: Someone muddles hands and feet when describing their work.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker does not put a hand in a foot; the reverse, a foot in hand, is the job of a chiropodist-like carer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicurist is someone who treats and beautifies people's feet.

clue.text: Tea in it? it's run out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the tea in there, or has it all gone?
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea urn is a large metal vessel for brewing tea in quantity.

clue.text: Barks at the horses

definitions.meaning: brown horses with black manes and tails

explanation.surface: A dog yaps at the horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To bay is to howl like a dog; bays are reddish-brown horses.

clue.text: Mutant newts in river, it's put around

indicators.note: a mutant is changed in form, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: Genetically altered amphibians are spreading in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mutant' rearranges NEWTS with R.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means scattered, spread about over an area.
